question.text: Which options generally have the HIGHEST vega (most sensitive to volatility changes)?

explanation.text: The Logic: Vega measures the change in option premium per unit change in implied volatility. Two effects combine: more time to expiry gives volatility more opportunity to impact the underlying, and ATM strikes carry the most extrinsic value to be re-priced when volatility shifts. The intersection — longer-dated ATM options — therefore typically shows the highest vega, while short-dated and deep-ITM/OTM contracts have lower vega. The Trap: Shorter-dated options have less time for volatility to act on the underlying and so have lower vega. Deep ITM/OTM options are dominated by intrinsic value (or near-zero value) and are less sensitive to volatility than ATM. Note: The cited NISM-Series-VIII workbook pages (76, 78, 81) support volatility/time effects and ATM uncertainty, but the explicit ranking "longer-dated ATM options have the highest Vega" was not located in the pages checked. The framing above is general options-Greeks theory rather than a direct workbook citation.
